version.changelog: Initial release: Real-time Indonesia earthquake monitor with detailed Moment Tensor support.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: bmkg-monitor
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is benign. It focuses on fetching earthquake data from official BMKG (Badan Meteorologi, Klimatologi, dan Geofisika) endpoints (`data.bmkg.go.id`, `static.bmkg.go.id`) using the `requests` library in `scripts/get_gempa.py`. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the agent in `SKILL.md`. All actions are aligned with the stated purpose of monitoring seismic activity.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its stated purpose (fetching BMKG earthquake data) and request no credentials or unusual privileges; only minor usability/quality issues were found.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (BMKG Monitor) align with the actual behavior: the script fetches JSON/text from BMKG endpoints (data.bmkg.go.id and static.bmkg.go.id) and formats earthquake information. No unrelated services, binaries, or credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running the included Python script with sane, narrow modes (latest, felt, recent, detail). The script only performs HTTP GETs against BMKG and prints results. Minor issues: SKILL.md and the script include a small inconsistency/typo — the 'latest' mode prints tip links containing a literal <EVENT_ID> instead of inserting an event identifier; the script does not read any local files, environment variables, or other system state beyond command-line args.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), so nothing is written to disk by an installer. The provided script depends on the Python 'requests' package but no install step declares this; that is a runtime dependency / usability issue, not a security mismatch.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no credentials, and the code does not access secrets or configuration files. Network calls are limited to BMKG official domains (expected for this purpose).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills/system settings. It only runs when invoked and prints fetched data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and safe for its stated purpose: it fetches earthquake data from BMKG and formats it. Before running: (1) review the script (you already have it) and confirm the endpoints (data.bmkg.go.id and static.bmkg.go.id) are acceptable for your environment; (2) ensure the Python 'requests' package is installed or install it in a controlled environment; (3) be aware of a minor bug/typo where example tip links include a literal <EVENT_ID> placeholder — the detail mode accepts an event id and will fetch the corresponding static files, but the printed tips in 'latest' won't substitute the id; (4) as with any downloaded script, run it in a trusted runtime (or sandbox) if you have any doubts about origin. Overall there are no unexpected credential requests or hidden endpoints.
